accepted.s: The Prior Informed Consent (PIC) procedure under the Rotterdam Convention implies that:
o: An importing country must agree before a listed chemical is exported to it
Only the exporting country can prohibit the use of a chemical
Chemicals may be exported only after approval by the World Health Organization
An exporting country may export any chemical without notification
accepted.x: Under the PIC procedure, the importing country must provide consent before a listed hazardous chemical can be exported to it.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise obligation attached to the treaty mechanism.
accepted.sec: Rotterdam Convention - PIC procedure, chemicals listed

accepted.s:
With reference to the Rotterdam Convention, consider the following statements:
1. It entered into force in 2004.
2. India acceded to it in 2005.
3. Its Annex III contains only industrial chemicals and excludes pesticides.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Convention entered into force in 2004 and India acceded to it in 2005. Annex III includes both pesticides and industrial chemicals that have been banned or severely restricted, making statement 3 false.
accepted.tq: Find the false statement by checking the restrictive word ‘only’.
accepted.sec: Rotterdam Convention - PIC procedure, chemicals listed

accepted.s: In India, which of the following combinations correctly identifies the Designated National Authorities for the Rotterdam Convention and its Official Contact Points, respectively?
o: Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilisers and Ministry of Agriculture; MoEF&CC
Ministry of Agriculture; Ministry of Environment, Agriculture and Chemicals
accepted.x: India’s Designated National Authorities are the Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilisers and the Ministry of Agriculture, while the Official Contact Points are located in MoEF&CC.
accepted.tq: Match institutions with their specific treaty roles.
accepted.sec: Rotterdam Convention - PIC procedure, chemicals listed

accepted.s: The Basel, Rotterdam and Stockholm conventions share:
o: A common financial mechanism administered by the IMF
A joint secretariat under the WHO
A common enforcement tribunal under the WTO
accepted.x: The Basel, Rotterdam and Stockholm conventions share one joint secretariat under the United Nations Environment Programme.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the responsible international body from nearby global institutions.
accepted.sec: Rotterdam Convention - PIC procedure, chemicals listed

accepted.s: In India, the Basel, Rotterdam and Stockholm conventions are coordinated by the:
o: Hazardous Substances Management Division of MoEFCC
Ministry of Agriculture’s Plant Protection Division
accepted.x: In India, coordination of these three conventions is undertaken by the Hazardous Substances Management Division of MoEFCC.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘who performs this job?’ approach for institutional questions.
accepted.sec: Rotterdam Convention - PIC procedure, chemicals listed

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Vienna Convention and the Montreal Protocol:
1. The Vienna Convention was adopted in 1985.
2. The Vienna Convention is a framework treaty dealing with cooperation, research, monitoring and protective measures.
3. The Montreal Protocol, adopted in 1987, is the action treaty adopted under the Vienna Convention.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Vienna Convention provides the framework, while the Montreal Protocol supplies the specific phase-out action adopted under that framework.
accepted.tq: Separate a framework treaty from the action treaty implemented under it.
accepted.sec: Vienna Convention 1985 and India Cooling Action Plan

accepted.s: The time horizon of the India Cooling Action Plan extends up to:
accepted.x: ICAP has a 20-year horizon extending to 2037-38.
accepted.tq: Read the terminal year carefully rather than choosing a familiar policy target year.
accepted.sec: Vienna Convention 1985 and India Cooling Action Plan

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT one of the six thematic areas of the India Cooling Action Plan?
accepted.x: The six thematic areas are space cooling in buildings, cold chain, servicing sector, domestic or indigenous production, research and development, and transport. Coal-based power generation is not one of them.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the stated thematic list.
accepted.sec: Vienna Convention 1985 and India Cooling Action Plan

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the ICAP target for reducing cooling demand by 2037-38?
accepted.x: ICAP aims to reduce cooling demand by 20–25% by 2037-38.
accepted.tq: Match each numerical target with the correct demand category.
accepted.sec: Vienna Convention 1985 and India Cooling Action Plan

accepted.s: Which of the following is the target of the India Cooling Action Plan with respect to cooling energy demand by 2037-38?
accepted.x: ICAP targets a 25–40% reduction in cooling energy demand by 2037-38.
accepted.tq: Compare overlapping percentage ranges without reversing the target category.
accepted.sec: Vienna Convention 1985 and India Cooling Action Plan

accepted.s: The India Cooling Action Plan proposes to train how many servicing technicians by 2037-38?
accepted.x: One of the ICAP targets is to train 1 lakh servicing technicians by 2037-38.
accepted.tq: Convert the policy figure into its exact quantitative form.
accepted.sec: Vienna Convention 1985 and India Cooling Action Plan

accepted.s: The Ozone Cell established by MoEFCC functions as India’s:
o: National Ozone Unit for phasing out ozone-depleting substances
National authority for hazardous waste transport under Basel only
National authority for regulating genetically modified crops
National disaster response agency for polar events
accepted.x: The Ozone Cell is India’s National Ozone Unit for the phase-out of ozone-depleting substances.
accepted.tq: Match an institutional name with its precise mandate.
accepted.sec: Vienna Convention 1985 and India Cooling Action Plan

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about atmospheric ozone:
1. About 90% of atmospheric ozone lies in the stratosphere.
2. The principal ozone-rich region lies approximately between 10 and 50 km in altitude.
3. The peak ozone zone is approximately at 25–30 km.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: About 90% of ozone is in the stratosphere, the ozone-rich region extends approximately from 10 to 50 km, and peak concentration occurs around 25–30 km.
accepted.tq: Combine percentage, range and peak-value statements in one atmospheric profile.
accepted.sec: Ozone layer - location, unit, ozone-oxygen cycle

accepted.s: The thickness or total column amount of ozone in the atmosphere is expressed in:
accepted.x: Ozone concentration in an atmospheric column is measured in Dobson Units (DU).
accepted.tq: Discriminate among scientific units by their measured quantity.
accepted.sec: Ozone layer - location, unit, ozone-oxygen cycle

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly represents the ozone–oxygen or Chapman cycle?
o: O2 is split by UV, oxygen atoms combine with O2 to form O3, and O3 absorbs UV and dissociates
O3 combines with nitrogen to form O2, which is then converted into methane
O2 absorbs infrared radiation and directly forms carbon dioxide
Ozone is formed only by the action of pollutants in the troposphere
accepted.x: Ultraviolet radiation splits O2 into free oxygen atoms; these combine with O2 to form O3, which absorbs UV and can split back into oxygen molecules and atoms.
accepted.tq: Follow the chemical sequence from initiating radiation to the regenerated products.
accepted.sec: Ozone layer - location, unit, ozone-oxygen cycle

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes stratospheric ozone from ground-level ozone?
o: Ground-level ozone protects living organisms from UV-B, whereas stratospheric ozone is a pollutant
Stratospheric ozone is formed from NOx and VOCs near the surface, whereas ground-level ozone is formed naturally in the polar vortex
Stratospheric ozone absorbs harmful UV-B, whereas ground-level ozone is a pollutant formed from NOx and VOCs in sunlight
Both forms are produced only by volcanic eruptions
accepted.x: Stratospheric ozone provides UV-B protection. Ground-level ozone is a pollutant produced through reactions involving nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds in sunlight.
accepted.tq: Separate two similar terms by location, formation and environmental effect.
accepted.sec: Ozone layer - location, unit, ozone-oxygen cycle

accepted.s: The seasonal thinning of the ozone layer over Antarctica is most pronounced during:
o: Southern Hemisphere autumn, March to May
Southern Hemisphere summer, December to February
Southern Hemisphere spring, approximately August to November
Northern Hemisphere spring, March to May
accepted.x: The Antarctic ozone hole is a seasonal phenomenon, with maximum thinning during Southern Hemisphere spring, approximately August to November.
accepted.tq: Link the phenomenon with the correct hemisphere and season.
accepted.sec: Ozone hole - location, season, PSCs, recovery

accepted.s: Polar stratospheric clouds contribute to ozone destruction because they:
o: Absorb all incoming solar radiation before it reaches the stratosphere
Convert oxygen directly into carbon dioxide
Prevent the return of sunlight to the polar vortex
Convert stable chlorine compounds into active forms on their surfaces in extreme cold
accepted.x: In the extremely cold polar vortex, polar stratospheric clouds provide surfaces that convert stable chlorine into active forms. When sunlight returns, these forms catalytically destroy ozone.
accepted.tq: Identify the causal mechanism rather than merely the associated location.
accepted.sec: Ozone hole - location, season, PSCs, recovery

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Antarctic ozone hole:
1. It was first detected over Antarctica in the mid-1980s.
2. A British survey reported it in 1985.
3. Its seasonal thinning is unrelated to the return of sunlight after the polar winter.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The ozone hole was detected over Antarctica in the mid-1980s, and a British survey reported it in 1985. The return of sunlight is important in activating chlorine-driven ozone destruction, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the known seasonal mechanism.
accepted.sec: Ozone hole - location, season, PSCs, recovery

accepted.s: The Antarctic ozone hole in 2025 peaked at just over 21 million square kilometres. This was:
o: Above the 2006 record of 29 million square kilometres
Below the 2006 record of 29 million square kilometres
accepted.x: The 2025 ozone hole peaked at just over 21 million square kilometres, well below the 2006 record of 29 million square kilometres, and closed early.
accepted.tq: Compare the current figure with the historical record instead of reading the absolute value alone.
accepted.sec: Ozone hole - location, season, PSCs, recovery

accepted.s: According to the projected recovery schedule, the ozone layer is expected to return to 1980 levels in most of the world by:
accepted.x: Recovery to 1980 levels is projected by 2040 for most of the world, by 2045 for the Arctic and by 2066 for Antarctica.
accepted.tq: Match each region with its distinct recovery year.
accepted.sec: Ozone hole - location, season, PSCs, recovery

accepted.s: The projected year for recovery of the ozone layer to 1980 levels over Antarctica is:
accepted.x: Antarctic recovery is projected for 2066, later than recovery in most of the world and the Arctic.
accepted.tq: Use the regional comparison to identify the latest projected year.
accepted.sec: Ozone hole - location, season, PSCs, recovery

accepted.s: A 1% loss of stratospheric ozone is associated with approximately what change in harmful ultraviolet radiation?
accepted.x: A 1% loss of ozone is associated with an approximately 2% increase in harmful UV radiation.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the percentage change in ozone from the resulting percentage change in UV exposure.
accepted.sec: UV radiation effects - target-wise

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT identified as a human-health effect of increased harmful ultraviolet radiation?
accepted.x: The listed human-health effects are skin cancer, cataract, blindness and suppressed immunity. Increased bone density is not included among them.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the target-wise effect list.
accepted.sec: UV radiation effects - target-wise

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the effects of increased UV-B radiation on crops:
1. It can reduce growth and photosynthesis in rice, wheat, corn and soybean.
2. A 1% rise in UV-B may reduce food output by approximately 1%.
3. It invariably increases crop productivity by stimulating photosynthesis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Increased UV-B can reduce growth and photosynthesis in the listed crops, and a 1% rise may reduce food output by about 1%. It does not invariably increase productivity.
accepted.tq: Identify the extreme and reversed claim in the crop-impact statements.
accepted.sec: UV radiation effects - target-wise

accepted.s: Damage to phytoplankton and larvae of fish, shrimp and crabs due to increased UV radiation can primarily lead to:
o: Increased ozone formation in the troposphere
Expansion of the stratospheric ozone layer
Immediate formation of polar stratospheric clouds
accepted.x: Damage to plankton and aquatic larvae affects the base and links of marine food chains, causing food-chain disruption.
accepted.tq: Trace the ecological effect from the affected organism to the ecosystem-level consequence.
accepted.sec: UV radiation effects - target-wise

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a material with the effect of increased ultraviolet radiation?
o: Wood, plastic, rubber and fabrics — degradation
Plastic and rubber — enhanced durability in all conditions
Wood and fabrics — conversion into phytoplankton
accepted.x: Increased UV radiation degrades materials such as wood, plastic, rubber and fabrics.
accepted.tq: Match the target category with its specific environmental effect.
accepted.sec: UV radiation effects - target-wise

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Kyoto Protocol — greenhouse gas cuts by developed countries
2. Basel Convention — transboundary movement of hazardous waste
3. Cartagena Protocol — biosafety relating to living modified organisms under the Convention on Biological Diversity
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Kyoto addresses greenhouse-gas cuts by developed countries, Basel concerns transboundary hazardous waste movement, and Cartagena concerns biosafety and living modified organisms under the CBD.
accepted.tq: Match each treaty with its distinctive environmental subject.
accepted.sec: Environmental treaties - focus identification

accepted.s:
Arrange the following treaties in chronological order of adoption:
A. Kyoto Protocol
B. Basel Convention
C. Cartagena Protocol
D. Vienna Convention
accepted.x: The Vienna Convention was adopted in 1985, the Basel Convention in 1989, the Kyoto Protocol in 1997 and the Cartagena Protocol in 2000.
accepted.tq: Place the earliest framework treaty first, then order the remaining treaties by year.
accepted.sec: Environmental treaties - focus identification
